content: We associate with each word $x_i$ three additional variables (denoted $c_i$): the indices of the beginning and end of the last completed chunk before $x_i$, and its label. For example, in Fig. FIGREF8, $c_4=\langle 3, 3, \text{VP}\rangle $ for $x_4=\text{the}$. Chunks, $c$ are only used as conditioning context via $p(x_i \mid x_{<i}, c_{\leqslant i})$; they are not predicted. Because the $c$ labels depend on the entire sentence through the CRF chunker, conditioning each word's probability on any $c_i$ means that our model is, strictly speaking, not a language model, and it can no longer be meaningfully evaluated using perplexity.
